look_here_first: Turn a leafy side branch OVER. The small oblong leaves sit in two rows and make a simple branch look like a compound leaf. At the leaf axils beneath it, look for nearly stalkless round capsules (fruit stalk usually under 0.5 mm), about 2–2.2 mm wide; use a hand lens. Long-stalked phyllanthus (P. tenellus) has fruit hanging on conspicuously longer stalks, often 5–10 mm. Do not ID either plant from foliage alone.

field_sequence: Recognize: annual herb roughly 10–50 cm high with many thin lateral branchlets, each lined with two ranks of small oblong leaves; the leafy twig, not one compound leaf, bears the fruits.
Look closer: check the underside of a fertile branchlet for small rounded capsules almost touching the stem; compare several nodes rather than one immature fruit.

Confirm: mature capsules about 2–2.2 mm wide and sometimes finely bumpy; with magnification, seeds about 1.1–1.2 mm have transverse ridges. Seed characters are not expected in an ordinary whole-plant photograph.
Leaf check: lateral-branch leaves typically about 6–25 mm long and 2–9 mm wide; tiny flowers may be inconspicuous.
morphology_keys.crew_warning: A fruit-free seedling or distant photograph may be Phyllanthus sp.; capture the underside and measure a fruit stalk before species-level confirmation.

field_comparison_matrix.diagnostic: Capsules nearly sessile, with stalk usually <0.5 mm; two-ranked branchlet leaves; fruit roughly 2 mm across.
field_comparison_matrix.field_action: Turn branchlet over and photograph a mature capsule attachment with ruler.

field_comparison_matrix.diagnostic: Capsules hang on obvious slender stalks, often 5–10 mm long; more wiry stems and papery leaves.
field_comparison_matrix.field_action: Measure stalk from branchlet to capsule; don't confuse a leaf stalk with the fruit stalk.

comparisons.crew_key: Underside fruit attachment is the tie-breaker, not the plant's general 'mini-mimosa' look.
